"When this enters the arena, NAME A CARD. Turn all cards with that name in banished zones face-down. ... At the start of your turn, put this into your SOUL."

The naming was CHOOSE with a choice_type and no `options`, so the handler returned immediately and nothing was ever named. The flip was a second ability on ON_BECOME whose FLIP_REF and REF_EXISTS both named a ref ("banished") that no effect on this card sets -- so it was gated on nothing and acted on nothing. And the last clause was PUT_SELF_BOTTOM_DECK where the card says the SOUL: the bottom of the deck is a different zone with different consequences (soul count feeds other cards; a deck card is drawn again).

A reference scope lasts ONE ability execution, so the named card is also stamped on the object; that is what lets a later clause read it.

NOT implemented, and recorded rather than approximated: "whenever a card with that name is banished WHILE THIS IS IN THE ARENA, turn that card face-down". effect_keywords.banish() already emits its event, so the hook exists, but there is no ON_BANISH trigger name wired to the DSL. Definition of done: that trigger exists and this clause becomes a FLIP_MATCHING over the banished card, gated on name_ref.
